speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed; introduces himself as President of Defence Aerospace)
quote: So we're seeing pricing pressures, and that's caused us to drive significant and aggressive cost reductions in recent years through our business. ... And we continue to drive cost base production to sustain returns in the level of 15% to 17% return on sales.
finding: In his earlier Defence role he met customer price pressure with aggressive cost reduction to hold a stated 15-17% return on sales, a pattern of cost-led margin defence he carried into Civil.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed; introduces himself as President of Defence Aerospace)
quote: So clearly, we're seeing some very positive intent. And I think we just need to see how that converts into policy and action, but clearly some positive mood music.
finding: Waits for policy and action to firm up before acting on signals (the 2016 US election and defence spending): 'wait until it's real'.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed; introduces himself as President of Defence Aerospace)
quote: And to this end, we're investing heavily in both products technology, to show we have a competitive product when those competitions arise; and also in our operational capability to ensure we have our competitive facilities from which to deliver those products.
finding: Invests in technology and facilities ahead of competitions so a credible product exists when a campaign opens, the same 'ticket to the game' logic he later applied to UltraFan.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: We're entering a less intense period of new product introduction, a greater proportion of our engineering talent and horsepower being applied to engineering maturity and cost reductions. And also, driving a more capital-light approach utilizing partnerships -- facilitated by partnerships where applicable.
finding: Shifts engineering spend from new engines to maturing and de-costing existing ones, and prefers partnerships to keep future programmes capital-light.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: And our 2024 outlook, which we gave yesterday is a reflection of that. But of course, it's not the destination, it's the next step in the journey. We will continue to improve beyond that.
finding: Frames guidance as a floor and a waypoint ('not the destination'), signalling further upside without committing to numbers beyond the outlook; a phrase he repeated in Q&A.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: One was the disruption we were causing with the durability issues on the Trent 1000. That disruption is now behind ... us, and we've made very good progress in validating and implementing permanent fixes to those issues
finding: Owns the Trent 1000 durability disruption as Rolls-Royce's doing and declares it over in May 2022; in Nov 2023 his successor still described the Trent 1000 coming out of an intense check-and-repair programme only by the end of the medium-term plan.

numbers.claim: Trent 1000 disruption behind us, permanent fixes being implemented
numbers.later_evidence: 2023-11 Watson: Trent 1000 intense check-and-repair continues to end of medium-term plan (~2027)

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: I'm confident that the cost reductions we've achieved will be substantially sustainable as our load returns, and we will get that gearing that Warren mentioned.
finding: A dated commitment (May 2022) that pandemic cost cuts would stick as volumes recovered, giving operating leverage; the slice does not show the outcome, but the next leadership reset targets in Nov 2023.

numbers.claim: cost reductions substantially sustainable as load returns

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: we anticipate like most market commentators and based on our own fleet by fleet, customer by customer analysis that flying hours on the passenger market will recover in 2024.
finding: Forecast made from bottom-up fleet analysis but anchored to consensus; passenger flying hours back to 2019 levels in 2024.

numbers.forecast: passenger engine flying hours recover to 2019 level

speaker: Unknown Executive (attributed to Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace)
quote: just the phasing, depending on the actual reality of any market opportunity, which is going to be well into the 2030s we'd anticipate on widebody and now it is 2030s on narrowbody too.
finding: A dated forecast that new-airframe opportunities for UltraFan are 'well into the 2030s' for widebody and 2030s for narrowbody; earlier (2016) Schulz had linked UltraFan to 2025 deliveries, so the timeline had slipped about a decade.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: I think actually our biggest exposure currently is on the pay inflation. But of course, the guidance and an outlook we've given, we made that with full consideration of the inflation environment we're in.
finding: Names the specific residual exposure (pay inflation) and states that the 2024 outlook already absorbs inflation, defending the guidance rather than hedging it.

numbers.claim: 2024 outlook set with full consideration of inflation

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: the pandemic, which caused the biggest restructuring in our history. We took out some GBP 1.3 billion of cost at the group level, that value dominated by the savings we'll describe in Civil Aerospace.
finding: Answered COVID with deep structural cost removal, most of it in Civil Aerospace, and presents the size of the cut as a credential.
trigger: COVID-19 collapse in flying hours (2020)
response: Largest restructuring in company history, ~GBP 1.3bn cost out

speaker: Unknown Executive (probably Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace)
quote: And clearly, our reputation took a knock on the statement on the 787. We've worked very closely with those customers through that period or for disruption. But the way we handled it through the disruption has now at least got some credit in the way we treated customers through that period
finding: Admits the Trent 1000 hurt Rolls-Royce's reputation on the 787 and claims credit for how customers were handled; speaker is labelled 'Unknown Executive' and attributed to Cholerton as the Civil president answering a programme question.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: When the pandemic started, we took tough decisions at pace and executed the largest restructuring in our history and completed ahead of schedule.
finding: Values speed and execution under crisis; describes his response to COVID as fast and finished ahead of plan.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: Secondly, services cost reduction. Dominic will talk about this, and you'll see more of this in the tours, but making sure engines last longer on wing and when they do come off wing spending less money on them.
finding: Puts time on wing and shop-visit cost at the centre of services margin, and hands the detail to his services head.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: I started this role at the start of 2018 and as well as the operational ramp-up we're focused on, clearly we're also driving and focused on productivity and efficiency, which has been a good start for when the pandemic hit.
finding: Took the Civil seat in 2018 running two agendas at once, the widebody production ramp-up and productivity, and frames the efficiency work as preceding the pandemic rather than forced by it.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: So with that now behind us, I look forward with optimism. Because as our market recovers, the better operational gearing from the cost reductions we've made, we're focused on sustainable cash generation and margin expansion
finding: After the Trent 1000 and COVID shocks, ranks sustainable cash generation and margin expansion above growth or share as the Civil priorities.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: And when we put an engine on aircraft, we capture, through its life, about 90% of the services value. We have deep customer relationships with great longevity. And as the engines mature, both industrially and technically, tremendous opportunity to take out costs and increase margins.
finding: Sees the business as an installed-base annuity: value comes from capturing lifetime services and maturing engines down the cost curve, not from new engine sales.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: And importantly, as we look through the life cycle, adapting our servicing -- services scope and making sure pricing truly reflects the value we bring. We're out of launch pricing phase. So frankly, we're also looking to operate with greater commercial edge.
finding: Signals a turn from launch-phase discounting to tougher LTSA and service pricing as the Trent fleets mature: an early form of the 'terms' lever.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: In our wide-body portfolio, we power 4 of the 5 of the new widebodies, all 4 of those, which are actually in service, with 3 sole-source positions with Airbus.
finding: Defines Rolls-Royce's position by widebody coverage and highlights its sole-source dependence on Airbus platforms as a strength.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: And the larger size, our UltraFan technology demonstrator, which is at the heart of our strategy for future widebody and indeed any future narrowbody opportunities.
finding: Positions UltraFan as a demonstrator serving both a future widebody and an optional narrowbody re-entry, rather than a committed product.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: I should stress that the UltraFan technology demonstrator, yes, it can -- it positions all the technology for future large engine applications, but also has technology which can add value to our existing engines.
finding: Justifies UltraFan spend partly by near-term spin-offs into the current Trent fleet, hedging the case if no new airframe arrives soon.

speaker: Unknown Executive (attributed to Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace)
quote: When you've got that technology and put so much money into it, you want to ... across the biggest possible market opportunity. ... So our ambition would be enter into narrowbody to better utilize over a wider ... technology. The opportunity isn't there just yet.
finding: States a narrowbody re-entry ambition in 2022, framed as amortising UltraFan technology over a bigger market, but explicitly not yet actionable.

speaker: Unknown Executive (attributed to Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace)
quote: And we'll no doubt do execute that as we have in many of our -- all our Trent programs actually in partnership, so we start to think of the sort of partnerships that might be valuable to us for that opportunity in our strategic planning.
finding: Assumes any narrowbody entry would be done with partners, as on all Trent programmes; partnership is the default structure, not the exception.

speaker: Unknown Executive (attributed to Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace)
quote: So we're -- we've chosen to invest well ahead of a market need because you need to put demonstration of technology, showing you got a ticket to the game with customers is absolutely critical.
finding: Accepts demonstrator spend well ahead of any launch because airframers demand proven technology; transcript labels the speaker 'Unknown Executive' but he refers back to UltraFan 'as I described', matching Cholerton's presentation.
trigger: Analyst asked what aircraft programmes UltraFan needs and the realistic path to narrowbody

speaker: Unknown Executive (attributed to Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace)
quote: But we have to invest now and demonstrate it, want to feed the technology to our existing engines, but also because this is complex stuff and we need to understand our risks early so that we can then better adjust the phasing of investment.
finding: Uses the demonstrator to retire technical risk early and keeps the main investment phasing flexible: invest in proof now, commit the full programme only when a market is real.

speaker: Unknown Executive (probably Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace)
quote: So we put a lot of money into making this engine as it should have been. And we have that -- there's closed customer relationships. So we intend to keep pushing and we know our share is low. We're not going to do anything silly, of course, on pricing to do so.
finding: Will compete to win back 787 share but refuses to buy share with price, even on a programme where share is low; speaker attribution probable, not printed.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: Inflation, clearly, we're not immune, obviously. But we do think, overall, we have reasonable protection. ... And I think our pricing escalation is always at least as good as the cost escalation.
finding: Relies on contract escalation formulae on both the supplier and customer side (OE and LTSA) to pass inflation through; sees inflation as manageable rather than a threat to guidance.
trigger: Analyst question on inflation and pricing formulae

speaker: Unknown Executive (attributed to Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace)
quote: And in the -- this point beyond, as I said in -- when I spoke, it's not the destination, clearly, we know we need to further improve returns. And our ambition will be to approach the returns enjoyed by our competitors as our engines further mature.
finding: Openly benchmarks Rolls-Royce's returns below its engine rivals' and sets closing that gap as the ambition; self-reference to 'not the destination' identifies the speaker as Cholerton.

speaker: Chris Cholerton, President of Civil Aerospace
quote: Very clear accountability for ownership of connecting activity to results in financial results and improvement results in the business. And after challenging norms so hard through our restructuring, and achieving those results, a greater belief that ambitious targets can be met and exceeded, and that will stick with us and be very valuable.
finding: Describes the culture he wants as clear individual accountability tied to financial results, and treats the restructuring as proof that stretch targets are achievable.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We must only invest in new technologies where we are differentiated, where the market opportunity is sufficiently large and where there is a viable ... business model and synergies with our existing activities.
finding: Sets an explicit four-part gate for new-technology investment (differentiation, market size, a viable business model, synergy), which he later applies to UltraFan and the narrowbody.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: we will centrally allocate capital to the most attractive market spaces or programs. This is a change from the past when there was more autonomy within the individual businesses. ... we cannot continue to allocate capital to projects that have low returns.
finding: Moves capital allocation from divisions to the centre and rules out funding low-return projects.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: first, we are going to deleverage the balance sheet and get to investment grade. And then we are going to look to reestablish shareholder distributions, and then it will be between shareholder distributions and investment in the future, and we will make those choices.
finding: Sets a strict order for cash: deleverage to investment grade first, then distributions, and only after that weigh returns against growth investment.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: You are going to hear that business has delivered improved performance last year. However, you are then going to hear from me that these results are not good enough for a company like Rolls-Royce. We have higher expectations for this business
finding: In his first results he labelled improved numbers 'not good enough', resetting the bar instead of taking credit for the post-COVID recovery.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: For 2023, we expect to deliver operating profit of GBP 800 million to GBP 1 billion, which includes a benefit of GBP 100 million to GBP 200 million from targeted contract improvements ... We expect free cash flow of GBP 600 million to GBP 800 million
finding: His first guidance was set low: it was raised in July 2023 to GBP 1.2-1.4bn and the year closed at GBP 1.6bn profit and GBP 1.3bn free cash flow.
response: Raised to GBP 1.2-1.4bn OP / 0.9-1.0bn FCF (Aug 2023); actual GBP 1.6bn OP, GBP 1.3bn FCF (Feb 2024)

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: That is becoming a challenging thing for the whole industry. I'm talking about industry. And therefore, my view is actually that supply chain will only stabilize between 12 to 18 months
finding: His first supply-chain forecast (12-18 months) proved too early. He later stretched it to 'next year, maybe beyond' (Aug 2023), then to 18-24 months (Nov 2023, Feb and Aug 2024), and constraints were still present in mid-2025.
response: Horizon repeatedly extended; still 'industry-wide supply chain constraints' Jul 2025

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: we have averaged a return on capital employed of just 3.5%. We have also not had sufficient strategic clarity to make investment choices. Instead, we have been trying to keep too many options open.
finding: Faults the old company for keeping options open, which signals he will cut programmes and make hard portfolio choices.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: I'm chairing the weekly transformation planning group and the whole executive team will spend time together each month to focus on this. ... we have appointed a Chief Transformation Officer reporting to me directly.
finding: Runs the transformation centrally and personally, with a weekly CEO-chaired cadence and a transformation officer reporting straight to him.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Rolls-Royce has been underperforming for an extended period. Our 5-year TSR of negative 67% is evidence of this and shows this is not just a COVID issue. Cash generation is unsatisfactory, and our debt is still too high.
finding: Opens with a blunt diagnosis that cash and leverage, not COVID, are the problem, making cash and the balance sheet the first priorities.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Commercial optimization is about getting the right reward for the risks we take and the value we create for our customers. ... In Civil Aerospace, for example, we set up a task force to review all the large engine LTSA contracts.
finding: From his first weeks he treats LTSA terms as a lever to reprice risk, putting every large-engine service contract under review.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: I believe facts are there that we are uncompetitive. ... Our benchmarking study demonstrates clearly that we are underperforming on a like-for-like basis our competition.
finding: Uses external peer benchmarking to set targets and openly concedes that Rolls-Royce trails its competitors on a like-for-like basis.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: in any turnaround at least 3 things are very important, really get the organization to understand the reality and why they need to change. Second thing is get very clear strategy that you can make it relevant to everybody.
finding: Applies a fixed turnaround playbook from earlier roles: shared reality, a cascaded clear strategy, then tight performance management.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Next, we will target cash as an input, not as an outcome. ... Now group cash flow is an input into a framework, which is used to inform the divisional targets.
finding: Plans top-down from a group cash target: divisions get cash-constrained targets rather than bottom-up budgets.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: I don't want to give a time because, as you know, you hit the investment-grade metrics, then rating agencies need to get there. ... our first priority is to get to investment grade. After that, yes, we would like to reestablish dividend, absolutely.
finding: Will not put a date on investment grade but keeps it ahead of the dividend. All three agencies were at investment grade by Feb 2025 and distributions resumed for FY2024.
response: IG from all three agencies by Feb 2025; dividend reinstated for FY2024

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Progress on this so far has been slower than I would have liked due to the challenging environment. We are increasing our focus on this now.
finding: Admits a shortfall (working capital) plainly and pairs it with a step-up in effort rather than a denial.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Yes, I can totally see why it may come across sort of conservative. ... So we effectively, in our guidance, reflected some of the risk profile of external environment.
finding: Admits building external-risk cushions into guidance, which is why he tends to beat it.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We have applied for certification for the latest Trent 1000 fix, which will more than double the time-on-wing of that engine.
finding: Aug 2023 start of the Trent 1000 HPT-blade commitment. The certification target slipped from end-2023 through 2024 and Q1 2025, and the blade was certified in June 2025.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We now expect operating profit of GBP 1.2 billion to GBP 1.4 billion in '23 versus our old guidance of GBP 0.8 billion to GBP 1 billion. ... We now expect free cash flow of GBP 0.9 billion to GBP 1 billion in '23
finding: Mid-year raise of about 40%, and the full year still came in above the raised range at GBP 1.6bn OP and GBP 1.3bn FCF, a pattern of beating his own guidance.
response: Actual FY2023 OP GBP 1.6bn, FCF GBP 1.3bn

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: But the gross, without interventions, actually number was a lot because I've been heavily involved. I did at least 5 reviews with the team on that.
finding: Handled the two supplier fires hands-on, holding repeated reviews himself to cut the cash hit to GBP 150m.
trigger: Two supplier fires disrupting civil parts supply

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We have an onerous contract provision of GBP 1.4 billion. We must rebalance these contracts. ... I have personally spoken with each and every customer with which we have an onerous contract. Our immediate focus has been on the 6 most onerous airline customers
finding: Leads the renegotiation of loss-making airline contracts himself and targets the largest exposures first.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: If my true partner comes to me and says, this is really one-sided contract, Tufan. So you got 2 options, you call us not a partner and transactional, then I deal with you next 15 years on that basis. Or you come to the table, we resolve this.
finding: Frames contract renegotiation as a binary partnership test, implying that customers who refuse will be treated transactionally for the life of the fleet.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: It's not textbook language. It is my experience. I didn't learn strategy in textbooks, but I did it by doing. ... I don't like options management in business. If you don't have choices, you don't have a strategy.
finding: Signature conviction: strategy means closing options and exiting activities outright rather than keeping hedges alive.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: I don't think Civil Aerospace supply chain, gas turbine supply chain will stabilize anytime soon. I definitely expect that definitely next year, maybe beyond
finding: Six months after his first forecast he moves the date for supply-chain stabilisation back into 2024 or later.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Our immediate priority is to return to an investment-grade credit rating, then resume shareholder distributions. ... Of this, safety at the top remains our first priority, taking care of our people and products.
finding: Ranks his priorities: safety, then an investment-grade rating, then distributions.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: First, we are primarily focusing on the quality of earnings and cash, not market share. This impacts how we approach new and existing orders and contracts. ... This is a change in mindset. We are concentrating on profitable growth.
finding: States that he will give up order and market share where the economics are poor, a key input for engine-campaign pricing.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Fifth, we have a new pricing framework in place to ensure that all new and renewing contracts have a satisfactory level of profitability. All new and renewing contracts are now reviewed by the Investment Committee.
finding: Centralises sign-off of every new or renewing engine and service contract, with a minimum-profitability gate on deal terms.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: In the first half of the year, we also raised time and materials pricing for large engines by 12%. This contributed to first half results significantly.
finding: Is willing to push large aftermarket price rises (12% on large-engine T&M) quickly to rebuild margin.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: it is a technology demonstrator. You need to think about that way, okay. And it has 2 purposes. One is to position us well for the next generation of engines ... that is a big engine, so -- intentionally, because we will scale down to wide body even to narrow body. It is scalable.
finding: Treats UltraFan as an option-creating demonstrator that can be scaled to widebody or narrowbody. Its technology also feeds time-on-wing fixes on current engines.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: I'm not going to give you a payback period right now because next-generation aircraft is not going to happen before 2030, and we need airframers, obviously, to go there first. But I will say this. We won't do anything not profitable. I will say that categorically.
finding: Will not commit to a next-generation engine until airframers launch an aircraft (not before 2030), and makes profitability a hard condition.

finding: Sees the engine maker's 15-20-year service relationship as deeper than the airframer's one-off sale, and uses that to justify renegotiating with airlines.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director

finding: Sees his job as setting the tone so that commercial teams press customers hard, knowing the CEO will back them.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director

finding: Treats surplus cash flexibly, choosing between buybacks and investment based on share price and the outlook.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: They are a milestone on our journey, not our final destination. ... our progress in the coming years will be progressive, but not linear year-on-year.
finding: Signature framing: targets are milestones, not destinations, and he warns that progress will not be linear.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director

finding: Nov 2023: promised Trent 1000 certification in 2024 and put the remaining step with Boeing and the FAA. It slipped to June 2025.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Investment grade, we talked about profile because that is in our hands, which we can create that profile. We are not a rating agency. Therefore, we cannot rate ourselves.
finding: Commits only to what management controls (an investment-grade profile), not to the agencies' timing. All three agencies were at investment grade by Feb 2025.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
