finding: Nov 2023 reset of the supply-chain horizon to 18-24 months, longer than the 12-18 months he gave in Feb 2023.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We power 1/3 of the wide-body aircraft in service today. And in 2022, more than half of new deliveries in the industry were powered by Rolls-Royce engines. However, this growth along a '22 margins -- 2022 margins would only drive a small fraction of the improvement.
finding: Treats widebody share growth as worth little unless each engine earns more, so margin per unit comes before volume.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: UltraFan is distinctive, developed to be competitive in the wide-body and narrow-body segments. ... The suite of UltraFan technologies delivered a 10% efficiency improvements on the most efficient engine available today.
finding: Positions UltraFan as a scalable platform for both segments, 10% better than the Trent XWB-84, and so as his ticket back into the narrowbody market.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: In Civil Aerospace, we believe we are well positioned to reenter the narrow-body market. By choosing a partnership approach for the next program, our UltraFan technology is a vital step towards this. At the right time, with the right partner, we will decide the next steps.
finding: First formal statement of the narrowbody re-entry: partner-led, UltraFan-based, with timing and partner left open.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: implementing a new value-driven pricing strategy to our new and renewing contracts as well as addressing onerous and low-margin contracts. And finally, driving rigor on contractual terms and conditions.
finding: His LTSA 'six levers' include value-based pricing and strict enforcement of contract terms, so he will trade customer goodwill for margin.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Yes, we are seeing financially, I think sort of to derisk things a little bit, partnership approach will be a good approach for the next generation. Obviously, partnership needs to work. If it doesn't work, we can consider alternatives because we are actually bringing a technology into this.
finding: Prefers a partner to share narrowbody risk but keeps a solo or alternative route as leverage, since Rolls-Royce brings the technology.
trigger: Analyst recalled Rolls-Royce leaving Pratt/IAE and passing on the geared turbofan, and asked why it chose to partner so early

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: that business model actually works well if you price the risk well. So because who is complaining in a high interest rate environment, getting the cash in advance. But it comes with a risk profile that you need to price well.
finding: Accepts the long-term risk of the power-by-the-hour model only if it is priced in, which shapes how he sets LTSA terms.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: So going into COVID, Rolls-Royce had 0.9. I run lots of businesses in my career. I never seen 0.9. ... You don't need COVID. You need a good recession. We are going to be in negative territory, right?
finding: Judges risk by operating leverage (cash cost to gross margin, TCC/GM). A ratio near 1 is unacceptable to him, so he halves fixed costs before taking on growth risk.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: To deliver these numbers and grow beyond that, we don't need to answer narrow body. It is an opportunity. ... And if it is not profitable, we won't do it because we don't need to do it.
finding: Narrowbody re-entry is optional, not existential, so he will walk away if the economics fail.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: I never called duopoly very competitive place, but the economics books will disagree with you, I think. ... But we are the probably only one who can go in.
finding: Sees the narrowbody engine market as a profitable duopoly (CFM and Pratt & Whitney) that only Rolls-Royce can credibly enter.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Last year, by the end of last year, it was going to be certified. Unfortunately, it didn't and it got delayed. And this year, we now -- we are working with both Boeing and FAA. Frankly, I was there, I met meetings a month ago with both Dave Cardon and the new head of FAA
finding: Admits the missed Trent 1000 date directly and shows he escalated it personally to Boeing and FAA leadership.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Don't look at every discrete year. We have midterm targets. ... Some years, that will mean you over deliver. Some other years may offset that a little bit. ... So this is the opposite of hockey stick.
finding: Steers investors to cumulative, front-loaded delivery rather than year-by-year results.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: This time last year, we set guidance ahead of expectations as our actions supported 25% uplift to the plans we started with. Then at the half year, we upgraded guidance by around 40% ... Double what was in Rolls-Royce plans less than 18 months ago.
finding: Builds credibility by pointing to repeated upgrades and results double the inherited plan.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We are working on the final stages with Boeing and the FAA on certifying the new [Audio Gap] double the engines time on wing. We expect it to be approved this year taking us to a competitive level of durability by next year, while the reliability remains very strong.
finding: Feb 2024 repeat of the Trent 1000 certification promise ('this year'). It slipped again, to June 2025.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: last year, in the last 15 years, we record orders for Rolls-Royce. We got 700 engines. ... So I think our pricing position is all about remunerating the value we create and creating win-win solutions as a result of that.
finding: Uses record orders as evidence that value pricing has not cost volume.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: When you want more efficiency, it comes with higher temperature and so on, and therefore, cycle time is lower. So no, I think no engine we will produce Trent 700 cycle time. But what we are doing with our engines, taking them to a very competitive level, okay, in any environment.
finding: Accepts that fuel-efficient engines trade away durability, so the goal is competitive time on wing priced into contracts, not Trent 700-level life.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: XWB824 is the best engine right now, durability, reliability and fuel efficiency in widebody market without any doubt, and you can ask any customer.
finding: Calls the Trent XWB-84 the benchmark widebody engine and uses it as the reference point for all durability fixes.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: So I think we are very aligned with Airbus. First of all, I should say. ... it's not an ambition. We are actually -- we have been implementing it. So it is an implementation for good 12 months. ... And obviously, we have similar situation with Boeing.
finding: Insists that his higher engine pricing is already in place and accepted by Airbus and Boeing, dismissing airframer complaints.
trigger: Airbus had said widebody engine pricing competition was challenging

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: This progress allows us to announce today that we will reinstate shareholder distributions for full year 2024 results. This will be based on a 30% payout ratio of underlying profit after tax for the full year 2024.
finding: Restarted distributions once the balance-sheet sequence allowed it, with a 30% payout ratio.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: And while we are progressing UltraFan with small engine as well, some additional funding comes with it because it is a different space. So there are some advantages of that as well.
finding: Uses outside funding to lower the cost of the narrowbody UltraFan demonstrator.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Actually, I've seen this movie before. ... Therefore, it won't be linear. I know that. And -- but front-end delivery obviously derisk, I would argue, our midterm target delivery.
finding: Signature phrase. He presents early over-delivery as a known pattern from earlier turnarounds that de-risks the medium-term targets.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Frankly, we didn't cause any issues. We were 1 engine behind first half, okay, 1 engine, 7000. So literally 1 engine, I can say it. So therefore, there is no -- I mean there is no issue we cause to any air framers, frankly.
finding: Plays down airframer criticism of Trent 7000 deliveries, defending Rolls-Royce's record rather than conceding.
trigger: Airbus comments in June 2024 about Trent 7000 supply

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: in our guidance in February, we knew a little, but not to the extent that we would actually say GBP 150 million to GBP 200 million. ... Therefore, we didn't talk about it because we don't want to talk about small numbers.
finding: Holds back emerging bad news until it is quantified and material, then discloses it alongside offsetting upgrades.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Our LTSA margins increased for all engine types, except the Trent 1000, which we expect to improve in the second half.
finding: Names the Trent 1000 as the one engine still diluting LTSA margins.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Actually, just yesterday, we did the first flight test very successfully. ... We expect the improved HPT blade for the certified by the FAA later this year.
finding: Aug 2024 repeat of 'later this year' Trent 1000 certification. It slipped to Q1, then Q2 2025, and the blade was certified in June 2025.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We now expect operating profit of GBP 2.1 billion, GBP 2.3 billion. This compares to our previous operating profit guidance of GBP 1.7 billion to GBP 2 billion.
finding: Second straight mid-year raise; the full year reached about GBP 2.5bn, above the raised range.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Yes, because of prolonged supply chain, yes, we said 18 to 24 months, I don't -- we keep managing these things very closely, but I don't have a crystal ball to say this is it. So about 18 to 24 months, yes, it prolonged.
finding: Admits the supply-chain horizon has slipped again and declines to give a firm date.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Why are we going with the demonstrator? Because, frankly, that doesn't mean we don't want to partner, but that means we would like -- we don't want to wait and position ourselves well out there.
finding: Invests ahead in a demonstrator to strengthen his hand in partner talks rather than waiting for a partner.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Our focus is on 15 suppliers whose delivery performance requires focused interventions. ... We also created a dedicated multidisciplinary agile team focused solely on resolving part supply issues.
finding: Manages the supply crisis by triaging specific suppliers and setting up a dedicated parts team, not by waiting for the market to recover.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: If you look at our order book or Airbus, Boeing order books, you will conclude that's not -- demand is not the issue, but actually supply chain is the issue to deliver that. ... I may point out our strategy was very deliberate to play big in India and China.
finding: Sees supply, not demand, as the binding constraint, and has deliberately bet on growth in India and China.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: sometimes people think because of our pricing actions, we are losing contracts, et cetera. That's not true, actually. ... we are remunerating our pricing actions is the investments we make and the risks we take. In the past, Rolls-Royce didn't actually price that fairly and we are right now.
finding: Rejects the idea that his pricing cost campaigns, and argues that past Rolls-Royce pricing undercharged for risk.
trigger: British Airways chose the GE engine over the Trent 1000 for its 787s

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: There's no change of strategy. We are pretty consistent company. We deliver what we say. ... we said narrowbody is something attractive for us, and we will participate preferably with partnerships. Nothing has changed in that.
finding: Rejects the idea that the narrowbody demonstrator means a solo strategy: partnership is still preferred.
trigger: Analyst asked whether moving ahead with a narrowbody demonstrator meant going it alone

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: UltraFan is 10% more efficient than that. And actually, at plane level, we believe you can get to 15% efficiency doing some other things on the plane combination. And IPs we have on UltraFan, a coverage of them and the duration of them positions us well.
finding: Bases the narrowbody case on UltraFan's efficiency margin and patent coverage around the geared design.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: So our issue with Trent 1000 is not reliability. It is -- reliability of this engine is as good as the competitor engine, but time-on-wing has been the issue
finding: Puts the Trent 1000's gap against GE's GEnx down to durability alone, a problem he believes can be fixed with investment.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: do we believe we can regain market share? Absolutely. Otherwise, we wouldn't have invested in time on wing. That is the only thing holding us back.
finding: Ties the GBP 1bn time-on-wing spend explicitly to winning back 787 share from GE.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We now have a strong balance sheet with an investment-grade rating from all three agencies. In addition to reinstating the dividend, we are also announcing a GBP 1 billion share buyback, Rolls-Royce's first in a decade to be completed this year.
finding: Completed his stated sequence (investment grade, then dividend, then buyback) within about two years.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We also made the decision to shut down our electric advanced air mobility activities alongside our electrolyser and fuel cell activities.
finding: Follows through on cutting non-core bets outright, consistent with his 'no options management' stance.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Finally, we expect to deliver an 18% to 21% return on capital in the midterm, highlighting the economic value creation potential of the business. I believe this will be one of the leading returns in the industry.
finding: Sets return on capital as the headline value metric and positions it against industry peers.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: There is a growth potential that's immense, but that's immense with proper returns, right? So there is lots of rigor, there is lots of challenge, but there is never hold back.
finding: Signature investment stance: no ceiling on growth spending as long as each project clears return scrutiny.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: if we had low return business, low-margin business, frankly, we are already getting out of them. So therefore, that opportunity, organic or inorganic may come from many places, and we will evaluate the way Helen talked about.
finding: Leaves the door open to acquisitions within the capital framework while continuing to exit low-return activities.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: I mean it's very simple. Boeing start 2 months, that delayed around 2 months. ... we said it first half, 1Q, then frankly, Boeing's strike sort of happened. And we couldn't continue with the flight test.
finding: Explains the latest Trent 1000 slip as an external cause (the Boeing strike) and states it briefly.
trigger: Analyst asked why Trent 1000 certification had moved from Q1 to Q2 2025

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: For example, 80% time on wing, we know that, otherwise, we wouldn't share with you other 40%, right? So there is no technology risk there, for example.
finding: Discloses a target only once he believes its technical risk has been removed.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Based on our 2025 guidance, we now expect to reach our CMD targets for profit and cash 2 years earlier than expected.
finding: The Nov 2023 medium-term commitments were delivered about two years early.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: At the CMD, we set out our target of delivering a 40% increase in time on wing across our modern engines by the end of 2027. We now believe we can achieve double this time on the time on wing improvement within the same period
finding: Doubles a durability target only once he is confident of it (40% to 80%). By Jul 2025 more than half was delivered or secured.
response: Jul 2025: more than half of the 80% delivered or secured

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: On Trent 1000, we are in the final stages of the certification of our new HPT blade that will more than double the time on wing of this engine. Flight testing was successfully completed. We have switched our OE production to the new blade already and are aiming for certification in 2Q.
finding: Final reset of the Trent 1000 date (Q2 2025), which was met with certification in June 2025.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We target an operating profit of GBP 3.6 billion to GBP 3.9 billion in the midterm ... Our midterm operating margin target is 15% to 17%.
finding: Upgraded 2028 targets set after the earlier ones were met early.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: The largest improvement will come from civil aerospace where we target an 18% to 20% margin in the midterm. We see the potential for this business to deliver a higher than 20% margin beyond the midterm.
finding: Sets a Civil margin target and an explicit ambition above 20% beyond 2028. H1 2025 underlying Civil was already about 19%.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: And the main issue with Trent 1000, I know this precedes my time definitely, there are lots of noises about this. Reliability of this engine is as good as the next. Our main issue has been time on wing. And we are effectively fixing it for good and we know it works.
finding: Puts the Trent 1000 problem down to inherited history and narrows it to time on wing, projecting a permanent fix.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Over the past 2 years, we have captured more than 50% of total widebody deliveries. This means our market share of the widebody installed base has risen from 32% in 2022 to 36% last year.
finding: Widebody share rose even under value pricing, which supports his claim that pricing did not cost volume.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Our contract margin is improving by 17 percentage point between 2022 and 2028 due to new and renegotiated contracts that are coming in at higher margins and better terms as well as the operational improvements that we are making.
finding: Quantifies the LTSA terms lever: new and renegotiated contracts carry much higher margins.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Yes, we are looking to increase the share on 787. Why not? Because this is going to be a highly competitive product. That's why we focused on that.
finding: Sees fixing durability as the route to winning back 787 share from GE.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We are very well positioned on narrowbody. Therefore, everybody is talking to us and we are talking to everybody. So I said it in CMD, our preference is partnership. We don't need partnership for capability, but our preference is that.
finding: Frames partnership as a choice, not a need, keeping solo re-entry as a credible option in talks with all parties.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: You put a contingency against that because it's not 100% certainty that you will. If you effectively execute that, which we have been doing so far, you actually release the contingency.
finding: Builds contingencies into contract accounting for technical risk, so on-time delivery produces upside.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: UltraFan is more efficient engine, as I said, than any other engine available in the market at this point in time. And the IPs we have on that on a geared structure is very favorable. Let me put it that way.
finding: Pitches UltraFan's geared architecture and patents as superior to both incumbents' routes (CFM's open fan and Pratt & Whitney's GTF).
trigger: Analyst noted the two narrowbody incumbents were taking very different technology routes

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We do it different than our competition. Our competition goes with long times, a lot longer than we put on LLPs. We go, here is the limit, and only when we understand operational with high fidelity, we sort of raised the limit
finding: Engineering conservatism: Rolls-Royce sets tighter life limits on life-limited parts (LLPs) than rivals and extends them only with data.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: a very granular strategy, that cascades into 17 strategic programs, whole company. If you are working for Rolls-Royce, you are working one of those programs. So you know your role, right? By resourcing, time on wing is one of them.
finding: Runs the company through 17 cascaded, resourced programmes with clear individual accountability.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: we allocated GBP 1 billion investment in 4 years. This is not like we are talking about UltraFan development. This is not like in 15 years GBP 1 billion.
finding: Favours fast-payback durability spending (GBP 1bn over 2023-27) and sets it apart from long-dated UltraFan programme spend.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Because they now know when we commit something, we honor it. We are that company. We don't commit that easily. ... So until I am sure we will deliver, I'm not committing.
finding: Signature stance: makes few commitments and treats each one as binding, presenting customer 'noise' as the cost of that discipline.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: today's financials are today's financials. I worry about tomorrow's financials. And as long as you continue to improve the business, underlying performance, tomorrow's financials will be secured.
finding: Signature phrase: focuses on future earnings power over current results.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: But there are big risks that we need to be thoughtful. Therefore, I'm thinking, Ben, maybe it's too early to talk about midterm targets
finding: Declines to raise the 2028 targets despite running ahead, citing tariff and supply risks, in line with his rule of committing only when sure.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Strong first half delivery gives us confidence to raise our 2025 guidance. We now expect underlying operating profit of GBP 3.1 billion to GBP 3.2 billion with a year-on-year improvement in all core divisions.
finding: Third consecutive mid-year raise (from GBP 2.7-2.9bn), continuing his pattern of conservative initial guidance.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We have now renegotiated all of our OE contracts, which means that our business aviation OE deliveries are now profitable. We remain on track for the Trent XWB installed engine deliveries to be breakeven or positive by the midterm.
finding: Has completed the OE repricing and is still on track for his commitment of break-even Trent XWB installed engines.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: The upgraded Trent 1000 HPT blade was certified in June, which will more than double the time on wing on these engines.
finding: Outcome: the Trent 1000 durability fix promised from 2023 was finally certified in June 2025, about 18 months after the first target.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: In February, we set a target of improving the time on wing of our in-production engines by more than 80% by the end of 2027. As a result of the progress we made to date, more than half of the targeted improvement is not delivered or secured.
finding: Reports early progress on the doubled durability target (the transcript's 'not delivered' reads as 'now delivered').

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: So once we do BoM C, so Trent 1000 time on wing program in a way is finished, and that will create by the end of this year, highly competitive engine.
finding: Commits to finishing the Trent 1000 durability programme (BoM C) by the end of 2025.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: In non-benign environments, we are going to double the time on wing. And in benign environments, we are going to increase time on wing by 50%. That is progressing, but that won't be completed before 2027.
finding: XWB-97 hot-and-harsh durability fix committed for 2027.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: some of our customers have been disappointed with Trent 1000 time on wing issues. And we have a big task force dealing with it. We actually have improved relations with customers.
finding: Accepts customer frustration over Trent 1000 durability but denies that his tough renegotiations damaged relationships.
trigger: Analyst said airlines and lessors were complaining that Rolls-Royce had become less accommodating

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We have been quick to react to the tariffs, where we have fully mitigated the drag impact across the group, as we transform Rolls-Royce into a more proactive, agile business.
finding: Responded quickly to the 2025 tariff shock and claims full mitigation.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: But at the same time, given constrained environment, some suppliers are able to increase their prices. ... No, we are not that company anymore. We are obviously reflecting that in our prices.
finding: Passes supplier cost inflation through to customer pricing rather than absorbing it.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: Every time I talk about it, we are not after a bunch of budget numbers. We are after improving the business every day.
finding: Steady priority from 2023 to 2025: continuous underlying improvement over hitting budget numbers.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: We are doing further tests on wide-body UltraFan just to progress that, at the same time, working on the demonstrator for narrow-body, which may take 2 years to build a demonstrator.
finding: Runs UltraFan on two tracks: widebody testing continues while a narrowbody demonstrator (about 2 years away) is built.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: The other angle is our preference continues to be partnerships. Therefore, we are in active dialogue with almost all the parties, I should say. So that is also progressing well. So that's where we are. I'm actually very optimistic definitely for the next generation of narrow-body and our participation in that
finding: Mid-2025: still partner-first on the narrowbody, talking to nearly all potential partners and openly optimistic about taking part.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO & Executive Director
quote: I always say sometimes our competitors, they issue 1 quarter I got 30% margin so that you cannot really look at, because our targets are sustainable targets as opposed to touch and go
finding: Contrasts his sustainable targets with rivals' one-off peak-quarter margins.

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: For the first time since a long, long time, we have had less order than deliveries within a year on either airframe or engines as it goes together normally. And clearly, this is a first. But it doesn't mean that we are anxious about the future of the market.
finding: Acknowledges a negative market signal (book-to-bill below one) but immediately frames it as a pause, not a threat.

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: Now there is a point of caution I want to give everybody is, as we will reach 50% of market share in the future within the next 3 or 4 years, we should expect to have more aircraft parked because this is just a sign of maturity.
finding: Forecast in 2016 a 50% widebody market share within 3-4 years; in 2023 Rolls-Royce reported a 55% widebody OE delivery share for 2022 but only 36% of installed engines.

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: you all know about the advance program, you all know about the UltraFan, this is preparing the 2025 deliveries from Rolls Royce and it's absolutely important.
finding: In 2016 he linked UltraFan to 2025 deliveries; by 2022 the Civil president placed UltraFan market opportunities 'well into the 2030s' (widebody) and in the 2030s (narrowbody).

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: I mean, this company, by 2020, will have beaten GE on the large engines. ... We will have beaten GE by 2020 in terms of market share and in terms of engine deliveries.
finding: A bold dated claim to overtake GE in large engines by 2020; it shows a share-led, rival-focused mindset that the later leadership replaced with margin focus.

numbers.claim: beat GE in large-engine market share and deliveries

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: I think coming from the airline industry, I can say that people understand that these are technological products, and sometimes, you have something you get surprised by. I think the reaction and the reactivity that the system has is the way you keep the customer with you or not.
finding: Accepts that in-service surprises happen and judges success by how fast the organisation reacts for the customer, drawing on his airline background.

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: So again, we are putting a lot of attention to the market, looking at this. It may not be anything. It might be a first sign of a slowdown. We don't know yet, but we are watching this.
finding: Watchful rather than reactive: he monitors early slowdown signals but takes no action until they are confirmed.

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: I look at 2016, we've done 24 Trent-powered transitions as compared to 10 last year at the same period. So clearly, we have accelerated. We have, as you probably know, we've been quite public with this, we've set up new switchers within Civil Aerospace to serve our customer and be more flexible, adaptive.
finding: Responded to parked Trent-powered 777s and A330s by building a dedicated transitions capability to move aircraft between operators and keep engines flying.
trigger: 2015 parking of Trent-powered 777s (Malaysia) and a customer bankruptcy

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: the first one is a ramp-up in capacity. We have a massive order book. We have to grow our capacity, especially on the large engines. And it's growth of about 20% year-over-year. ... Until a point where we reach a peak of about 600 large engines a year.
finding: Ranks the large-engine production ramp as his first priority, with a 20% a year growth path to a planned peak of about 600 large engines a year; by 2023 Rolls-Royce planned 300-350 widebody OE deliveries in the midterm.

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: Yes, we have reduced by more than 20% the level of override in Civil despite the fact that we are growing. But on top of this, it's more about changing the way we do business.
finding: Cut Civil overhead by more than 20% during growth and frames transformation as changing ways of working, not just cost-cutting.

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: So in 2015, we had about 3,500 engines in the world flying. And within 10 years, we will barely double that number. So this means we are doing a lot on aftermarket. We are doing a lot on the network to prepare it and to serve these engines because all of these engines will require maintenance.
finding: Anticipated the need to expand the MRO network to serve a fleet doubling within a decade: shop capacity as a growth constraint.

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: As you know, we have 3 programs in parallel that are -- that is unprecedented in Rolls-Royce, with 3 big programs, which are very, very close to each other, the Trent 7000, the Trent 1000-TEN and the Trent XWB 97k.
finding: Ran three new-engine programmes in parallel during a capacity ramp, a high schedule-risk load that preceded the Trent 1000 durability crisis.

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: our target is always to be better than the competition. So the if there is a 777 or if there is an A330 to be parked, I rather prefer to see a Pratt or GE aircraft being parked as compared to mine.
finding: Treats Pratt & Whitney and GE as direct rivals for every aircraft's utilisation and competes on keeping Trent-powered aircraft flying at their expense.

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: Boeing and Airbus, just to take these 2. I think they have been impacted and hit in their reputation, but also in their numbers ... they are asking for demonstration of technology. So it's no longer a world where you can show a nice PowerPoint. You need to show products.
finding: Reads airframer customers as burned by programme delays and now demanding demonstrated hardware before selecting an engine, which justifies demonstrator investment.

speaker: Eric Schulz, Former President of Civil Aerospace (title as printed)
quote: I mean, not having 3 people believing to be in charge who can make 180 degrees directions, but having one pilot on board and only one pilot in command at any time who is making decisions; consulting others, but making decisions.
finding: Wants single-point accountability: one decision-maker who consults but decides, replacing diffuse shared authority.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: We have a clear pathway back to a net cash position in the medium term. We have plenty of liquidity to manage the uncertain pace of the recovery in engine flying hours in the meantime.
finding: He set net cash as the medium-term balance-sheet destination in 2021. It was reached at end-2024 (GBP 0.5bn net cash) under his successor.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: And we won't stop investing in our current products. There are good near-term returns available from increasing durability and efficiency.
finding: Even while cutting costs he protected durability and efficiency spending on in-service engines as quick-payback investment, and repeated the line in February 2022.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: I'd reiterate the point around liquidity. Liquidity is there. There is plenty of liquidity. We're not dependent on engine flying hours recovering. So I don't see the need for any other nonorganic I think, measures.
finding: He ruled out further non-organic balance-sheet measures, relying on GBP 7.5bn of liquidity, disposals and organic cash to deleverage.
trigger: David Perry (JPMorgan) asked about next steps on the balance sheet after the ITP disposal

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: In terms of the forecast going forward, when do we get to 2019 levels? There are a lot of industry forecasts out there as to -- we can look at -- you can look out and rather than us adding our own. I'd encourage everyone to look at what the wider industry forecasts are.
finding: He declined to give the company's own flying-hours recovery forecast and pointed analysts to industry forecasts, avoiding exposure on variables he could not control.
trigger: Analyst asked when engine flying hours would return to 2019 levels

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: So sometimes when I see commentary on them, they're sort of viewed as something to ignore or to overlook. ... So we plan for cost savings, but we don't recognize them until we are sure of them and they start to flow through. ... I tend to look at long-term contracts
finding: He pushed back on investors discounting catch-ups. His accounting stance is conservative: savings are booked only once proven, and contracts are judged over their whole life.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: The disposals program is progressing well and we continue to target proceeds of at least GBP 2 billion. ... we will continue to do so in a measured way with plenty of liquidity, and there are no near-term pressures as we rebuild the balance sheet.
finding: He refused to be a forced seller and committed to at least GBP 2bn of disposals. Delivered: the programme completed in 2022, and the proceeds repaid GBP 2bn of debt (UKEF loan), as reported in February 2023.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: We continue to expect to turn free cash flow positive sometime during the second half of this year. We also expect a full year free cash outflow of around GBP 2 billion, which would represent an improvement of over GBP 2 billion on 2020.
finding: He reiterated a cautious 2021 guide of about GBP 2bn outflow. In December 2021 he guided to 'a little bit better than GBP 1.7 billion', and the actual figure was a GBP 1.5bn outflow, beating the guide by more than GBP 500m (GBP 300m of it concession timing).

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: Free cash flow of at least GBP 750 million is still achievable in a 12-month period when engine flying hours exceed 80% of 2019 levels. However, given the uncertain pace of recovery in international travel and looking at industry forecasts, it is unlikely that this will occur in 2022.
finding: This ties a cash threshold to flying hours: at least GBP 750m of FCF once EFH exceeds 80% of 2019. It proved conservative. 2022 (EFH 65%) still made GBP 505m, and 2023 (EFH 88%) made GBP 1.3bn.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: Our concession balance fell by GBP 239 million, which was lower than we planned for due to third-party deliveries moving out. Our strong liquidity position means we are not sensitive to the precise timing of the unwinding of these delayed concessions.
finding: On the 787/Trent 1000 concession outflows delayed by Boeing's delivery problems, he leaned on liquidity: timing slips were absorbed and not treated as a guidance driver.
trigger: Boeing 787 delivery delays shifting Trent 1000 concession payments

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: We continue to focus very heavily on the areas within our control and have seen substantial sustainable cost benefits from our restructuring program. We are well on the way to reducing the size of our Civil Aerospace business cost base by around 1/3.
finding: He focused on controllables: a structural one-third cut to the Civil cost base, to create operating leverage as flying hours returned.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: And what attracted me most is the opportunity to help fulfill that potential by very clearly delivering on the commitments we have made; by building a balanced, profitable and cash-generative business; by getting the balance sheet back into good shape; and by helping capture the demand and upside created by the energy transition.
finding: His opening agenda in the COVID recovery: hit commitments, build a balanced and cash-generative group, repair the balance sheet, and capture energy-transition growth. Civil is one part of a diversified group, not the centre.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: I very clearly heard 3 things in meeting our investors: One, make sure you deliver on the near-term commitments you've made; two, simplify financial reporting, make it easier for us to understand the business; and three, set achievable targets for the medium term and then achieve them or even beat them.
finding: His priorities were built from investor feedback after years of credibility damage: beatable targets, simpler reporting and near-term delivery. His guidance philosophy is to under-promise and over-deliver.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: Again, coming in, I look across at a better balanced group now, and I look at Defence and Power Systems and the opportunities there, the resilience and opportunities from energy transition and push hard around what those margins should be to be competitive within the marketplace. So I don't just look at civil.
finding: He took a portfolio view, pressing margins in Defence and Power Systems rather than focusing only on Civil. Civil was one of three earnings engines in his framing.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: I'm comfortable with the business model. It's a smart business model. In fact, many businesses that I've been -- I've worked with in the past would love to have a business model where you have your customers being effectively so sticky and then you can work hard on making sure you deliver at a sensible cost.
finding: He defended the LTSA power-by-the-hour model as structurally attractive (sticky customers), with the job being cost delivery rather than changing the model.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: And George, just something I'd probably add on the pricing point, and you can see it in the half year numbers where we've got some long-term contract catch-ups, which are the result of some of those commercial negotiations. So I'm a big believer in us being rewarded for the value that we bring
finding: On aftermarket terms he believes in value-based pricing and points to positive LTSA catch-ups as evidence that renegotiation is lifting contract margins.
trigger: Analyst question on pricing

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: Last year, that was a very challenging one for Rolls-Royce, and we were well supported by our investors, lenders and the U.K. EF. As a result, we have around GBP 3 billion of net debt today. That is too high. We will reduce it over the coming years.
finding: He judged post-COVID leverage unacceptable and committed to deleverage. Net debt including leases fell from GBP 5.2bn at end-2021 to GBP 3.3bn at end-2022 and GBP 2bn at end-2023, reaching net cash in 2024.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: The rule of thumb, as you called it, that we talked about just over a year ago, it's an okay approximation, and it was done at a point in time given the engine programs ... It's not one that I overly use within the business but not a bad thing to keep in mind.
finding: He accepted the roughly GBP 30m cash per 1% of flying hours sensitivity (the analyst's framing) as only an approximation. He added on the next page that lower flying hours also push shop-visit costs out, so the net cash hit is less than proportional.
trigger: Harry Breach (Stifel) asked whether the GBP 30m per 1% EFH rule of thumb still held

numbers.note: analyst-cited rule of thumb vs 2019 baseline

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: We are committed to rebuilding our balance sheet and returning to an investment grade credit profile in the medium term. ... A strong balance sheet is very important for us. We will balance the pace of that rebuild with the investment opportunities across our portfolio to make sure that we maximize the long-term return for our shareholders.
finding: He committed to an investment-grade profile in the medium term while explicitly trading the speed of deleveraging against investment. Outcome: Fitch and S&P investment grade by August 2024, and all three agencies by February 2025.

numbers.outcome: IG from 2 of 3 agencies by Aug 2024; all 3 by Feb 2025

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: There is a sort of a pivot away into some of those growth opportunities over the course of the next few years, probably a little bit away from civil and where the civil business is. And the increased level of investment, you better see them effectively in 3 places. So Defence, where we've got some big bids coming up
finding: Under the East/Kakoullis plan, incremental investment in 2022 tilted away from Civil towards Defence, Power Systems and New Markets. This is the opposite of the later narrowbody and UltraFan emphasis.
trigger: George Zhao (Bernstein) asked where increased investment would go

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: This needs to be done ground up, right? I'm not going to put something over the top for a sort of veneer in how I present because it's fundamental to how we run the business on a day-to-day basis
finding: He framed reporting simplification as aligned with internal value drivers, budgeting and remuneration rather than presentation. Transparency is treated as an operating discipline.
trigger: David Perry asked about simplifying reporting and making the business more investable

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: That's why we started talking about revenue. That's why we started talking about margin as well as cash and to come how we think about returns. So that's why that profit is there. I don't view it as missing guidance.
finding: He broadened guidance from cash only to revenue and margin, to reflect a 'balanced' group and to anchor consensus, after the analyst noted that explicit profit guidance was missing.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: We've exceeded our GBP 2 billion free cash flow guidance for 2021 by over GBP 500 million. And GBP 300 million of that was due to concession slippages, and we shared that with you in December. And I'm not going to claim any credit for that. That's not controllable.
finding: On a beat he separated controllable from uncontrollable drivers and refused credit for concession timing. This is a signature move that protects credibility for later.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: We expect to generate modestly positive free cash flow in 2022, representing a substantial improvement on 2021. Now that increase comes despite the concession slips that I mentioned earlier, going from '21 into '22.
finding: He guided to 'modestly positive' 2022 cash despite concession headwinds. 2022 delivered a GBP 505m inflow, another conservative guide beaten.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: The assumption we've made is that GBP 300 million slipped into '22 as you'll have seen. ... It's going to typically depend on deliveries. ... it's an uncontrollable. So I'm not going to claim credit for it, if it doesn't happen. And if it happens earlier, then we'll highlight it.
finding: Boeing 787 delivery delays kept moving Trent 1000 concession payments. He treated them as an uncontrollable, disclosed separately, and promised transparency in either direction.
trigger: Boeing 787 delivery halt delaying concession outflows

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: as we look to 2022, there is going to be a load increase in the Civil business. And seeing how that load increase manifests itself, think around about 30% more load going through that business. And when we look at it from an operating cash cost perspective, it's around about 6%.
finding: He quantified post-restructuring operating leverage in Civil: about 30% more workload for about 6% more operating cash cost.
trigger: Question on how restructuring supports the ramp-up

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: We're into the newer engine programs. ... They are earlier stage. We recognize less margin on those as they are less mature. There's a lot of margin left to come. And when I look at the balance sheet and I look at that long-term service agreement balance ... there are big chunks of that, that our potential margin
finding: His view of LTSA economics: new programmes (XWB, 7000, 1000) book low early margins, and the LTSA creditor holds latent margin to be released by cost savings and time on wing.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: 75% of our R&D investment in the medium-term will be on lower carbon technologies and making our existing products compatible with net-zero. We also continue to invest in improving the profitability of our products by increasing time on wing, efficiency and productivity. ... Around 80% of our CapEx and R&D this year will be focused on Civil, Power Systems and Defense.
finding: His investment allocation steered 75% of R&D to lower-carbon work while keeping 80% of capex and R&D in the established businesses, including time-on-wing work.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: Next, we very carefully consider the risk reward profile of each investment based on an estimate of its IRR in a range of scenarios. ... An example of an investment that will generate return in the near-term is the work we've done on extending the time on wing in the Trent 700 engine.
finding: He judges investments on scenario-tested IRR across a near/medium/long-term mix. Engine durability (Trent 700 time on wing) is the model near-term return, while long-dated bets (SMR, electrolysers) need higher risk-adjusted IRR.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: Now when I started this role, I set out 3 clear priorities for the business: deliver on our commitments, simplify how we report and invest wisely for the future.
finding: His signature triad, 'deliver on our commitments, simplify how we report, invest wisely', was repeated at every event from August 2021 and used as the scorecard he reports against.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: the importance of looking at catch-ups and what they are telling you because they are saying that over the life of those contracts, if it's a positive catch-up over the life of those contracts, we expect those to be more profitable going forward ... Works both ways. So we need to be balanced around that.
finding: He repeatedly taught investors to read catch-ups as lifetime-margin signals while acknowledging they can be negative (for example a GBP 22m Defence inflation charge). His message is balanced, not promotional.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: we also set out medium-term financial targets based on engine flying hours recovering to 2019 levels by around 2024. Within those targets, we expect a low double-digit compound annual growth rate in total revenues based on 2021 as the start year, a high single-digit operating margin and trading cash flow to comfortably exceed operating profit.
finding: He set Civil medium-term targets from the May 2022 Civil Investor Day. Large-engine EFH reached 101% of 2019 in H1 2024, and the Civil margin beat the target (11.6% in 2023, 16.6% in 2024) before the targets were superseded by the November 2023 CMD.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: back in Derby on the 13th of May, we sort of talked about in the medium-term being around about a GBP 500 million number on the LTSAs. It is going to be meaningfully more than that this year.
finding: He flagged upside to his own LTSA medium-term marker of about GBP 500m. 2022 delivered GBP 792m of net LTSA growth.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: you saw just over, I think, just over 400 in the first half, and we're guiding to around between 1,100 and 1,200 over the full year. And the big driver of that, frankly, is the engine flying hours growth. As that growth comes back, the shop visits follow.
finding: He guided to 1,100-1,200 total shop visits in 2022, but the actual figure was 1,044, a miss on an aftermarket volume metric that he tied to flying-hour recovery.
trigger: Analyst question on shop-visit outlook

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: Now at that time, we thought those would largely unwind in 2022. Since then, we've seen those further delays in 787 deliveries ... But there is a larger headwind coming in 2023 as those growth slips are compounded in '23 by continued low receipts from Trent 1000 new engine deliveries.
finding: He flagged the 787 concession headwind a year ahead. The 2023 guide later carried a GBP 200m legacy Boeing concession outflow, so the early warning proved accurate.
trigger: Continued Boeing 787 delivery delays

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: all investments over GBP 5 million are reviewed by our group investment review committee. That meets monthly, I've shared all of those meetings since I started with the business. We set a very high bar when considering new investments, and there are many examples of projects that didn't make the grade.
finding: He ran a centralised, monthly investment gate at a low GBP 5m threshold, with a high bar and in-flight reviews. Many projects were rejected.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: What if there was something very dramatic on China? We're not just going to wait to react to it, what can we do now to make sure we're in the right position.
finding: He favoured pre-emptive scenario planning (inflation, a China shock) at executive and board level over waiting to react.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: We focused on our supplier list, seeking to work with the very best performing suppliers. ... A case in point, titanium. We've already secured a long-term agreement with a U.S.-based titanium supplier, which means that we continue to be increasingly less reliant on titanium from Russia.
finding: After the invasion of Ukraine he cut supply risk through a consolidated supplier base, long-term agreements and a US titanium source in place of Russia.
trigger: Russia-Ukraine war and supply-chain inflation

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: That's a fancy way of saying we had a supplier conference and a 10% reduction in pricing going forward, and that gets locked in with very low levels of indexation.
finding: On the Pearl 10X he used spend consolidation to lock in a 10% part-price cut with low indexation. This is the procurement lever on new-engine unit cost.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: Civil delivered positive GBP 63 million of trading cash flow again, a significant GBP 1.1 billion higher than last year. With costs rebased, as volumes recover, we see Civil Aerospace becoming the cash engine for the group.
finding: He cast Civil as the group's future cash engine, driven by flying-hour recovery over a rebased cost structure rather than by new programmes.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: The catch-ups where they reflect strong execution and commercial discipline. That means we've got higher anticipated profitability across the life of these contracts going forward.
finding: He reads positive LTSA catch-ups as evidence of better lifetime contract margins from commercial discipline and execution.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: We set out 5 key value drivers for the business: one, maximize service receipts; two, reduce service costs; three, improve OE margins; four, grow business aviation; and five, make sure we benefit from a favorable point in the investment cycle as we exit what has been a period of intense product development.
finding: His Civil value drivers were harvest-mode: the aftermarket, cost, OE margin, and benefiting from the end of a heavy development cycle. No new-engine launch was implied.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: Firstly, through commercial discipline and on pricing and also on contract management. In Civil Aerospace, we've been able to contractually pass on higher input prices on both OE and aftermarket through indexation clauses.
finding: His response to inflation in Civil was to enforce indexation clauses on OE and aftermarket contracts. Terms are used defensively to protect margin.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: So the Civil Aerospace business, we are -- and I think you talked about enforcing indexation. We are being robust around how we do that. ... And a lot of those catch-ups are driven by the expectations through that enforcement. From a cash perspective, it actually comes a little bit -- it has a little bit of a lag
finding: Inflation pass-through in LTSAs shows up as profit catch-ups first, with cash following later. He is robust on enforcement but candid about the lag.
trigger: Robert Stallard (Vertical) asked whether indexation covered cost inflation

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: It's not a cap, it's a color. So up to a certain level, we can pass it on. Then there's a color of a couple -- 2 or 3 percentage points that we can't pass on. And then beyond that, what's called effectively a hyperinflationary clause kicks in, which means we can pass on again.
finding: LTSA escalation terms have a collar: inflation is passed through up to a level, a 2-3 point band is absorbed, and a hyperinflation clause restores pass-through above it. There is no ceiling, but customer negotiation is required.
trigger: George Zhao (Bernstein) asked whether LTSA indexation had a cap

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: we were carrying a very large hedge book, much larger than our peers. ... we found ourselves over hedged. ... Under our new approach, we're going to be carrying a smaller hedge book with a declining percentage of cover over a 5-year period, which will mean that market movements in foreign exchange will impact us sooner.
finding: He reacted to the GBP 1.7bn COVID over-hedge loss by shortening FX cover from a rolling 10-year to a 5-year declining profile, accepting earlier FX exposure in return for flexibility and peer comparability.
trigger: GBP 1.7bn COVID-era over-hedge close-out

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: The reopening of China towards the end of the year drove a further improvement in January, up to 79% of 2019 levels. This supports our expectations for large engine flying hours to be between 80% and 90% of 2019 levels as we move in 2023.
finding: He guided 2023 large-engine EFH to 80-90% of 2019. The actual figure was 88%, accurate and within range.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: For 2023, we expect between 1,200 and 1,300 total shop visits with a step-up in large engine shop visits as higher flying hours activity converts into increased demand for aftermarket services.
finding: He guided 2023 shop visits to 1,200-1,300. The actual figure was 1,227, with large-engine refurbs at 368 against 248, so the guide was accurate.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: In 2023, we expect the change in the LTSA balance to be between GBP 500 million and GBP 700 million, which reflects a slightly lower level of growth than in '22 due to an increased number of shop visits, including more wide-body refurbs. ... should result in contract catch-ups of between GBP 100 million and GBP 200 million.
finding: Mixed outcome. The LTSA guide was beaten (GBP 727m in H1 2023 alone; about GBP 1.1bn for the year), but 2023 catch-ups ended as a GBP 29m charge and net contractual margin was -GBP 54m once supply-chain costs were booked under his successor.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: We haven't given divisional guidance, so you didn't miss it. So the guidance we've given around operating profit is the GBP 800 million to GBP 1 billion for '23. And we've called out within that GBP 100 million to GBP 200 million of targeted contractual improvements.
finding: His last annual guide (2023 operating profit GBP 0.8-1.0bn) proved very conservative. The actual 2023 underlying operating profit was about GBP 1.6bn as the new CEO's transformation took hold.
trigger: Analyst asked for 2023 divisional guidance

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: Large spare engines represented 23% of total OE deliveries, which is higher than the usual 10% to 15% as we build the spare engine pool to underpin fleet health and improve resilience ahead of the anticipated increase in shop visits.
finding: He chose to build spare engines well above normal levels to support fleet health ahead of the shop-visit surge. Spares were used as a durability buffer.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: The year-on-year increase was driven by 3 things: firstly, improved profitability on LTSA contracts, reflecting commercial discipline on pricing, costs and contractual terms. This resulted in GBP 319 million of contract catch-ups in '22
finding: Civil's return to profit in 2022 rested on LTSA contract profitability from pricing, cost and terms discipline (GBP 319m of catch-ups).

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Executive Director
quote: The average earnings life term is a little bit lower than the number you said. It's closer to 8, 9 years rather than the 12. ... There's also effectively contract management. So how an engine is flowing? ... We're being much tougher on making sure the contractual terms are enforced within that.
finding: He put the remaining LTSA life at about 8-9 years and added contract enforcement (billing for actual operating profiles) to repricing as a margin lever.
trigger: Charlotte Keyworth (Barclays) asked about improving LTSA terms

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Director
quote: Our strong liquidity position enabled the cancellation of a GBP 1 billion bank facility in the first half that we deemed surplus to requirements. Our next debt maturity is a EUR 550 million bond loan note in 2024, which we expect to repay with underlying cash flows.
finding: He began shrinking surplus facilities and committed to repay the 2024 bond from cash. It was repaid in May 2024.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Director
quote: We expect Civil Aerospace's operating profit in the second half of the year to be broadly similar to the first half.
finding: His H2 2023 Civil call was accurate: H1 GBP 405m and full year GBP 850m imply about GBP 445m in H2.

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Director
quote: That growth reflected EFH growth and our commercial optimization actions, notably improved average rate per flying hour, driven by escalation and customer pricing negotiations. ... So of that GBP 727 million LTSA balance growth, approximately GBP 500 million benefited our cash flows in the period.
finding: He attributed LTSA cash to a higher rate per flying hour from escalation and negotiation, and was explicit that risk-and-revenue-sharing partners take a share (about GBP 500m of GBP 727m retained).

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Director
quote: Just from a profit perspective, LTSA margin recognition is based on forecasting your future costs. So that will have though your inflation concern would be built into those future costs. So that's the basis of that being recognized that's built in.
finding: He explained that LTSA margins already embed forecast cost inflation, so inflation risk shows up through re-estimates (catch-ups or onerous charges) rather than surprises.
trigger: Analyst concern about inflation in LTSA margins

speaker: Panos Kakoullis, CFO & Director
quote: We said there was more to come. Some of that came through in the first half, but there is still more to come. ... where we previously provided around some minimum utilization that we didn't think we would get that is now being built and will be collected.
finding: Contract enforcement extended to collecting overdue debts and billing minimum-utilisation clauses previously provided against. Existing LTSA terms were exploited fully.
trigger: Analyst question on overdue collections

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO & Director
quote: Our investment approach will be disciplined with spend targeting strategic growth, including the innovation and engineering excellence we are renowned for. We plan for CapEx and R&D to be above depreciation and amortization across the period. This compares to 2022 but it was approximately GBP 300 million below.
finding: She committed to reversing underinvestment, with capex plus R&D above D&A against about GBP 300m below in 2022. In February 2025 she restated it as 'average above D&A'. Engineering spend is funded from rising cash, but within discipline.

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO & Director
quote: Our capital frame is focused on 3 clear priorities: a strong balance sheet with an investment-grade profile, a commitment to growing shareholder returns ... Strengthening the balance sheet is a clear priority. We are positioning Rolls-Royce to better withstand volatility and external shocks and give us financial flexibility for the future.
finding: Her capital frame ranks the balance sheet first (an investment-grade profile and resilience to shocks), then growing returns, then disciplined investment. The ordering stayed the same in every later event.

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO & Director
quote: We have strict investment hurdle rates in the mid- to high teens for our 3 established divisions. We also have a group-wide investment committee process where Tufan and I review and sign off on all investment cases above GBP 25 million.
finding: This sets her investment threshold: hurdle rates in the mid-to-high teens, with every case above GBP 25m signed off jointly by her and the CEO. She restated it in August 2024. Engine programmes must clear return-based gates.

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO & Director
quote: R&D, indeed, the simplest way to hold that is we expect our gross R&D spend to be broadly flat over the period. Now the important thing to remember there, when I speak to R&D and CapEx is because of the actions that we're taking as part of our strategic review, our portfolio will be smaller and more focused.
finding: In 2023 she held gross R&D flat but concentrated on a smaller, more focused portfolio, while net investment rose by more than GBP 300m on 2022. New-engine money is redeployed rather than added.

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO & Director
quote: We're very clear that we will close those down through cash, and we have no intent of strengthening the balance sheet and getting back to that investment-grade profile by raising cash. So that is not our intent.
finding: She ruled out an equity raise or new borrowing to reach investment grade. Deleveraging was to be organic, from operating cash only.
trigger: Question on whether investment grade was the priority ahead of distributions and how debt would be handled

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO & Director
quote: we do expect year-on-year profit and cash growth, but can't necessarily take a straight line and draw it from '22 to '27. I don't think that's experience of how our transformations have gone in the past. And indeed, there's too many variables in there. ... it's most absolutely not back-end loaded.
finding: Her guidance style: commit to direction (growth every year) but refuse linear paths, while pre-empting the suspicion that delivery is back-loaded.
trigger: Analyst asked how non-linear the progression to midterm targets would be

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO & Director
quote: In the midterm, which we see as being around 2027, we are targeting between GBP 2.8 billion and GBP 3.1 billion of free cash flow, a growth of around GBP 2.5 billion compared to 2022.
finding: She set a 2027 free-cash-flow target that was overtaken within 15 months. 2024 free cash flow reached GBP 2.4bn, and in February 2025 the target was reset to GBP 4.2-4.5bn for 2028. Her pattern is targets that are beaten and then rebased upward.

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO & Director
quote: We expect the net Civil LTSA balance to grow between GBP 0.8 billion and GBP 1.2 billion per annum. This compares to a net growth of around GBP 800 million in 2022.
finding: She set the core aftermarket cash metric at GBP 0.8-1.2bn a year. Outcomes: 2023 came in about GBP 1.1bn. 2024 was about GBP 0.7bn, 'just below the lower end', because of Trent 1000 refurbs and the supply chain. 2025 was guided to the low end, and the 2028 target is the top end.

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO & Director
quote: we expect large engine flying hours to grow between 120% to 130% of 2019 levels by the midterm.
finding: Her November 2023 flying-hours assumption was raised to 130-140% of 2019 in February 2025. Large-engine flying hours reached 109% of 2019 in H1 2025. The traffic assumptions proved conservative.

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO & Director
quote: Insights like these have helped us design programs that will support the sustainable release of around GBP 2 billion of working capital benefits. The largest opportunity relates to inventories.
finding: She set a gross working-capital release target of GBP 2bn. GBP 0.4bn had been delivered by August 2024. 2024 released GBP 280m, with inventory days down more than 45 since the programme began, and in February 2025 she said there were plans to go further.

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO & Director
quote: Our cash flow growth will enable us to reduce our gross debt by paying down our near-term debt maturities as they fall due, namely the EUR 550 million bond in 2024 and the $1 billion bond in 2025.
finding: She committed to retire maturities from cash and kept the commitment. The EUR 550m bond was repaid in May 2024, and the $1bn bond was due to be repaid from cash in October 2025 (stated July 2025).

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO & Director
quote: When we are confident that the strength of the balance sheet is assured, we are committed to reinstating and growing shareholder distributions. Whilst we're not at this point today, we expect to be there in the near term.
